incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `cuda_alloc_failure` on service `gpu-runtime` (severity: P1). Trigger: repeated cudaMalloc failures & OOM kernels on node pool `gpupool-prod-4`

Oncall_Alice: omg seeing this on grafana. p50 latency spike + OOM events. tagging @Oncall_Ben and @SRE_Charlie.

Oncall_Ben: acked in PD. I'm booting dashboards now. any immediate customer impact?

SRE_Charlie: partial. A few requests failed with 502 from inference-edge, errors show `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in logs. Looks correlated to kvcache population on long-chat workloads.

Oncall_Alice: timeline: started ~1960123300 (10m ago) with a sudden KV cache hit-rate jump and sustained long sequences. Node gpupool-prod-4-b4 showing repeated kernel failures.

EngInfra_Dan: checking node-level dmesg and nvidia-smi. attaching quick outputs: ```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
15380 MiB, 16384 MiB
15390 MiB, 16384 MiB
...```

SRE_Charlie: also seeing this in runtime logs: ```2026-03-14T09:42:21Z ERROR kv_cache.cpp:412 cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)
2026-03-14T09:42:23Z WARN runtime_batcher.cpp:197 eviction failed, falling back to smaller batch
2026-03-14T09:42:24Z ERROR inference_worker.cpp:88 kernel launch failed: cuLaunchKernel -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

Oncall_Ben: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) disable prefix/KV cache on the model route (fast config flip), 2) lower max_batch_tokens or batch_size to reduce peak usage, 3) cordon and drain the most noisy nodes and force traffic away. Thoughts?

Oncall_Alice: flip 1) first. Patching route to turn off kvcache for `gptx-13b` can be done via console API: ```PATCH /routes/gptx-13b/config {"kvcache_enabled": false}``` I'll run if folks agree.

SRE_Charlie: +1 to disabling cache; it will increase tokens/cost but should free memory quickly. Also prepare rollout to reduce batch_size by 30%.

EngInfra_Dan: cordon command queued for gpupool-prod-4-b4 and gpupool-prod-4-c2: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --force`. Doing it one node at a time.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Oncall_Ben at 1960123468. Auto-escalation timer paused.

Oncall_Ben: executing PATCH now. sending request... ```curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"kvcache_enabled":false}' https://console.api.redwood/run/routes/gptx-13b/config``` Response: 200 OK.

Oncall_Alice: confirmed via API, kvcache disabled. Monitoring memory.

SRE_Charlie: memory usage dropping on the effected nodes. cuda OOM events decreased but still seeing occasional kernel failures. lowering batch_size next.

Oncall_Ben: rolling config: `max_batch_tokens: 1024 -> 700` on canary set (25% traffic). Command: ```PATCH /routes/gptx-13b/traffic {"canary_percent":25, "max_batch_tokens":700}```

EngInfra_Dan: draining node gpupool-prod-4-b4 complete. No new pods scheduled there. Next node c2 draining in 4m.

SRE_Charlie: logs after kvcache off and batch drop: ```2026-03-14T09:50:02Z INFO runtime_batcher.cpp: batch_size reduced, peak memory expected -28% 
2026-03-14T09:50:10Z INFO kv_cache.cpp: disabled by config
2026-03-14T09:50:37Z ERROR inference_worker.cpp: transient kernel error, retry succeeded
```

Oncall_Alice: customer impact: A handful of customers on heavy-chat saw slightly higher latency and a few 502s during spike window (~09:42-09:50 UTC). Product notified via status page: Status update queued.

Oncall_Ben: I'll post to #incidents after we stabilize with an incident summary. For now I leave this in-progress and handoff to @Oncall_Alice for overnight coverage if it resurfaces.

Oncall_Alice: handing off to Oncall_Ben? (we just need one of us) I'm staying on for 10m then passing to @Oncall_Ben.

Oncall_Ben: I'll take the handoff at 1960123600. Actions for oncoming: monitor OOM count, check for kernel retry rate, consider temporary route scaling (add more dedicated nodes) if recurs.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Escalation suppressed. Incident status: acknowledged -> in_progress.

SRE_Charlie: followup notes: likely root cause combination: sudden kvcache working set expansion from long-chats + aggressive batching caused memory fragmentation and intermittently failed cudaMalloc. Remediation: 1) avoid enabling kvcache on high-variance long-chat routes by default; 2) add soft-margin in batcher to prevent bursts; 3) improve OOM telemetry (report pre-OOM memory fragmentation). I'll open a ticket.

Oncall_Ben: created ticket SYS-1427 (postmortem + followups). I'll draft incident message.

Oncall_Alice: thanks team. leaving now, handoff completed at 1960123600. 

Oncall_Ben: confirmed takeover. Monitoring till 1960123699. Will update if anything changes. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note appended to thread.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident updated.

Oncall_Ben: closing thread for now — continuing monitoring. Summary will be posted in #incidents and triage ticket will track fixes.
